resources.string: AirPlay mirroring, made for your TV.
Connect your Apple device and TV to the same network.
Full screen for the details. PiP to keep watching while you use other apps. Press OK to show controls.
Floating mode asks for permission to display over other apps the first time you use it.
Floating permission granted. Use “PiP controls” to move the window, or reopen AirPlay PiP for full screen.

System PiP uses Android’s controls. Floating mode needs overlay permission. While watching HDMI, select “PiP controls” from the launcher, notification or Quick Settings (if supported). Move with the arrows; OK or Back releases the remote.
System PiP is not available or permitted on this device.
Allow display over other apps, then return and select Floating window again.
This TV does not expose overlay permission settings. Check the README for the optional ADB command.
Could not open floating mode. Check overlay permission and start screen mirroring first.
Use system PiP for an active visual session, only on devices that support it. Audio-only sessions stay in the background.
For floating mirroring only; system PiP position is managed by Android.
AirPlay PiP · Select “PiP controls” to move
Arrows: move · OK/Back: finish\nMenu: full screen · Releases after 15 s idle
No floating mirroring window is active. Start mirroring and choose Floating window first.
Could not select PiP. Use its notification or open AirPlay PiP.
Independent surface is the default for HDMI. If your TV displays it incorrectly, try TextureView. Both keep the same AirPlay session; HDMI compatibility depends on the TV.
Stop AirPlay, audio, downloads and floating windows, remove the notification and close the app. Your settings are kept.

Start mirroring first. Open controls now, or schedule them in 10 seconds so you can switch to HDMI. CPU compatibility uses a software Canvas at up to 10 FPS and 480 px per edge; it still needs the decoder and offscreen GPU.
CPU Canvas output only + controls in 10 s
No recent incoming frames (may be a still screen)
Input active, decoder not advancing. Try reconnecting mirroring.
Decoder active, offscreen GPU not advancing.
Decoded frames arrive but app output is stalled.
App buffers advancing; TV panel visibility is not verified.

Separate from floating output. Software and conservative hardware modes require their selected decoder type and disable HEVC; neither silently changes type. Conservative hardware omits vendor latency keys. Changes restart the active receiver; reconnect mirroring. Profiles are available in PiP controls.

Unlike CPU Canvas output, this changes the decoder itself. Selects a software H.264 component, disables HEVC, advertises 1280×720 at 24 FPS and uses CPU Canvas output. Saves these settings and restarts the receiver if active, interrupting mirroring and audio. Stop and reconnect mirroring from the Apple device, then open floating controls again. This is experimental and may use significant CPU; the TV must provide a compatible software decoder.
No compatible software H.264 decoder for 1280×720 was found. Settings were not changed.
Software H.264 profile saved. Once the receiver restarts (or after starting it), stop and reconnect screen mirroring from your Apple device.

Uses a hardware H.264 component at 1280×720/24 FPS, disables HEVC and removes vendor low-latency, adaptive maximum-size and forced color/frame-drop keys. Selects independent-surface output without CPU readback. The active receiver restarts and interrupts mirroring/audio; reconnect from the Apple device. This cannot reserve the VPU against HDMI or override TCL firmware. No silent software fallback.
No compatible hardware H.264 component for 1280×720 was found. Settings were not changed.
Conservative hardware profile saved. Stop and reconnect screen mirroring after restarting/starting the receiver. This is an experimental compatibility test, not a confirmed HDMI fix.
Temporarily upload a newer APK from a phone or computer on the same LAN. Android asks before installing.

Starts an opt-in local HTTP server on a temporary port. Only private/local clients are accepted. Choose a 4-digit one-time code or no-code mode. APK must be a newer io.github.airplaypip build signed with the installed app certificate. Android always asks before installing. HTTP is not encrypted; use only a trusted LAN.
Waiting for an APK upload. Keep AirPlay PiP open on the TV.
Server is running but no usable local IPv4 address was found.
APK is validated. Grant “Install unknown apps” for AirPlay PiP, then press Install update.
Opening Android installer for version %1$s. Confirm on the TV.
Android requires permission before AirPlay PiP can open an update. Installation still requires confirmation. You can turn off “Allow from this source” after updating.
APK verified and ready. Confirm the installation on the TV.
Installation was cancelled. The validated APK is still ready to retry.

NO-CODE MODE: any device on this private LAN can submit an APK. Package, version and signing-certificate checks still apply; Android will still ask before installation. Use only briefly on a trusted network.
Five incorrect codes were entered. Server stopped; start a new session to get another code.
Advertise a second, independent AirPlay name. Both senders can mirror at once when enabled; the TV and hardware must decode/composite both streams.
Select a screen to route its audio.
Two hardware video decoders may exceed the TV’s capacity. The TCL C715 still needs physical testing; start with low resolution/FPS.

Experimental per-app Bluetooth routing. Select a connected Bluetooth output for AirPlay while HDMI playback remains on the TV output. Android TV audio policy may override this preference; restore System default if no sound. Other apps are unaffected where the TV/firmware allows independent routing.

When decoder mode is Automatic, switch from hardware fullscreen to software H.264 when entering system or floating PiP, then back on return. Needs a new sender IDR/IRAP and software decoder support; may reduce resolution/FPS. Explicit Software or Hardware profiles are respected. Test before relying on HDMI.
